title: Vector DB fallback & dimensions discovery
summary: Intro call to understand Novara's vector search use case for clinical notes search. Main concerns: embedding dimensionality, throughput at 200 QPS, hybrid BM25+rerank design, VPC/private deployment, and security (SOC2/KMS). Agreed to run a 2-week pilot: Redwood hosted with dedicated capacity evaluation and an on-prem proof-of-concept for sensitive data. Action: Redwood to send pilot plan, security pack, and cost estimate; customer to share sample dataset and query profile.
action_items: Maya Chen; Send pilot plan + pricing + Redwood security pack (SOC2, ISO artifact links); due 2026-04-12
Tomás Alvarez; Share 10k sample docs + query distribution CSV; due 2026-04-13
Luca Grant; Prep throughput test script and suggested embedding dims (128/256/768) to evaluate; due 2026-04-14
Priya Nair; Confirm legal/regulatory list for private data to decide split of hosted vs on-prem; due 2026-04-16
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot and security materials
Customer to upload sample dataset to secure S3 link (pre-signed)
Plan a throughput benchmark run for hosted dedicated and private installer
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-09 13:00 EDT | Duration: 48 min | Attendees: Maya, Luca (Redwood) — Priya, Tomás, Daniel (Novara)

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya from Redwood, account exec on this. Quick intro?
00:12 - Priya Nair: Hey all, I'm Priya, I run search and relevance at Novara. We ingest clinical notes, structured EHR, looking to improve recall and ranking for clinician search flows.
00:25 - Daniel Reed: Daniel here, CTO, just sitting in to understand constraints from infra and compliance sides.
00:31 - Tomás Alvarez: Tomás, ML infra, I'll own the pilot work.
00:35 - Maya Chen: Great, Luca, do you want to add a quick tech note?
00:39 - Luca Grant: Yeah, hi, I'm Luca, solutions engineer. We'll focus on embeddings, rerank, latency/cost tradeoffs, and options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
00:48 - Priya Nair: Our primary ask: search must feel instant, under 200-300ms for clinician UI. We do a BM25 retrieval then an embedding rerank. Current system is CPU-only and slow. Looking to move to vector DB backed rerank.
00:59 - Maya Chen: Got it. What's target QPS for peak?
01:03 - Tomás Alvarez: For now, peaks about 150 QPS, we want headroom to 200 QPS. Average request returns 50 candidates from BM25 then rerank top 50.
01:13 - Luca Grant: That's helpful — so if you rerank 50 candidates per query at 200 QPS, that's 10k embeddings scored per second; we need to design for that throughput.
01:24 - Priya Nair: Right and cost matters, we can't have 10k full model calls per second to a large decoder, we want efficient vector score + small reranker.
01:33 - Daniel Reed: Also note we have regulatory constraints for some documents — certain PII-laden notes must stay on-prem.
01:39 - Maya Chen: Completely understood. We commonly do a hybrid split: store sensitive vectors in Private (on-prem or VPC), less-sensitive in Hosted. We can route requests by policy and do a federated search or local rerank.
01:53 - Tomás Alvarez: How does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching with the repeated queries pattern? We have many similar queries from the same clinician sessions.
02:02 - Luca Grant: We have continuous batching and a KV cache for transformer state; for embeddings/rerank it's usually per-request vector scoring, but we can cache embeddings for documents and frequently asked queries. The cache helps reduce compute if the same doc vectors are reused. Sometimes transcript mis-hear: "K-VK cache" appears in auto-caption.
02:20 - Priya Nair: Embedding dimensionality — our current embedding model outputs 768 dims. We've seen Pinecone costs blow up with that. Could we test lower dims?
02:29 - Luca Grant: Absolutely. We recommend experimenting with 128 and 256 dims for throughput/cost tradeoffs; for clinical semantics you may need 256/384 range. For reranking a smaller cross-encoder can operate on top of coarse vector hits.
02:43 - Tomás Alvarez: What kind of QPS can Dedicated capacity support for 256 dims? Ballpark GPU pool sizing?
02:50 - Luca Grant: Ballpark, with 1x A100-equivalent in Dedicated and optimized kernels, you can do several thousand sparse similarity ops per second with ANN index like HNSW; the limiting factor is often network + disk for large indexes. For pure scoring (CPU/GPU bound) we push KV vector ops through optimized kernels. We'll propose sizing in the pilot doc.
03:09 - Daniel Reed: We also need to understand persistency: if we snapshot vectors to object storage and warm indexes on nodes, what's the cold start time?
03:17 - Luca Grant: Cold starts depend on index size; for an index of 10M vectors at 256 dims, warm up can be minutes if we preload shards, or tens of minutes if we stream. Dedicate reserved nodes with preloaded shards minimize startup.
03:32 - Priya Nair: Hybrid search — we do BM25 then vector rerank. Is there value in reranking fewer candidates (like top 20) to hit latency targets?
03:41 - Maya Chen: Yes, many customers do 20-25 rerank to balance UX and cost. We can also cascade: cheap lexical rerank, then vector rerank on top results, then a small cross-encoder for final scoring.
03:53 - Tomás Alvarez: For the reranker, can we host an on-prem lightweight cross-encoder that calls Redwood's embedding store?
03:59 - Luca Grant: If you run Private deployment, the model and index live in your VPC/on-prem and calls never leave the network. For Hosted we can offer VPC peering or customer-managed keys (KMS) for encryption at rest. But if legal requires no egress, Private installer is the path.
04:13 - Priya Nair: Security pack — do you have SOC 2, ISO, pen test reports?
04:18 - Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send our security pack; SOC2 Type II, ISO artifacts, KMS integration docs, and our audit log capabilities. Also mention RBAC and SSO (SAML).
04:27 - Daniel Reed: Good. On cost: show me delta between Hosted token cost vs Dedicated reserved capacity — especially for 10k vector scores per second scenario.
04:37 - Luca Grant: We'll include a cost model in the pilot plan: tokens vs per-hour GPU pricing, plus network egress and index storage. Also, quantization/embedding reduction can lower memory and cost.
04:49 - Tomás Alvarez: Do you do productized rerank connectors to common vector DBs? We're evaluating Milvus and an in-house vector store; we don't want lock-in.
04:58 - Luca Grant: We have connectors and an API that works with many vector DBs. For Dedicated/Private we can run the runtime alongside Milvus/Weaviate or use Redwood's integrated ANN store. The integration pattern depends on whether you want Redwood to manage the index (hosted) or have your DB manage it.
05:12 - Priya Nair: We want a gradual approach — start Hosted for non-sensitive data, run benchmarks, and then test Private for the sensitive bucket.
05:20 - Maya Chen: That path is common. For the pilot we'll propose: 2 weeks Hosted dedicated evaluation with a backfill of your sample data, run throughput benchmarks at 50/100/200 QPS and dims [128,256,768], and a 1-week on-prem proof-of-concept for sensitive docs.
05:36 - Tomás Alvarez: Sounds good. How do we measure relevance regressions? We have a small eval set.
05:42 - Luca Grant: Bring your eval prompts and relevance labels; Redwood Optimize can run A/B and regression checks and tie to prompt sets. We'll include quality monitoring options.
05:51 - Priya Nair: For rerank, do you recommend ANN + exact re-score or full exact dot prod?
05:56 - Luca Grant: Typical: ANN (HNSW) for candidate retrieval then exact re-score on top-k; exact dot-prod on 20-50 items is cheap and gives best precision. ANN reduces memory and I/O.
06:08 - Daniel Reed: Any gotchas on VPC/private installer — firewall rules, node sizing, and upgrade path?
06:14 - Maya Chen: Installer requires outbound to control plane for telemetry by default but can be air-gapped with enterprise plan. We'll document firewall ports, KMS setup, and upgrade process.
06:25 - Tomás Alvarez: If we quantize embeddings to int8 or use PQ, will that affect nearest neighbor accuracy significantly for medical terms?
06:33 - Luca Grant: Some accuracy loss is possible; we'll test 128 vs 256 float32 vs quantized 8-bit. For clinical domain we might choose 256 float32 or 256 f16. We'll recommend an eval set to measure P@1/P@5.
06:46 - Priya Nair: We also need an SLA for tail latency — 95th percentile under 300ms.
06:52 - Maya Chen: For Dedicated we can commit to latency SLOs in the contract; for Hosted we have tiers. We'll include suggested autoscaling and burst capacity options in the pilot doc.
07:03 - Tomás Alvarez: What about index sharding and geo? We serve EU clinicians; need EU residency.
07:09 - Luca Grant: We can pin model and index regions. We recommend deploying EU shards for EU traffic and routing via smart routing policies.
07:19 - Daniel Reed: Any reference customers in regulated health?
07:23 - Maya Chen: We have a couple — we'll share anonymized case studies and an enterprise reference under NDA.
07:29 - Priya Nair: Questions from my side — do you support hybrid search where BM25 and vectors are fused in a single scoring pipeline?
07:36 - Luca Grant: Yes, we support hybrid scoring patterns; you can combine lexical and dense signals, and we can run a weighted combination or learning-to-rank on top.
07:46 - Tomás Alvarez: For monitoring, do you expose token-level and query-level cost metrics?
07:50 - Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-request cost and latency breakdown and model-level dashboards.
07:57 - Priya Nair: Great. Any immediate blockers?
08:00 - Daniel Reed: Only legal sign-off for data transfer for the non-sensitive set.
08:04 - Maya Chen: Ok we'll flag that in the next steps. We'll follow up with the pilot doc and security pack.
08:10 - Tomás Alvarez: We'll prepare the sample dataset and eval queries.
08:13 - Maya Chen: Perfect. Next steps recap?
08:16 - Maya Chen: Action items: Maya to send pilot + security pack; Luca to provide benchmark plan; Tomás to send sample data; Priya to confirm regulated doc list.
08:26 - Priya Nair: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
08:28 - Daniel Reed: Thanks, talk soon.
08:30 - Maya Chen: Thanks all, bye.

Notes: occasional imperfect transcription (e.g., "K-VK cache"), speaker overlaps in the first minutes, and some proper nouns mis-capitalized. Shared artifacts mentioned: deck link (https://redwood.example/pilot-deck), security pack (link to sent PDF), sample upload S3 pre-signed link to be created.
